schemaFit.detail: One blocking keyword. bakerPrice.price uses minimum:0 / maximum:2, and Anthropic lists minimum/maximum as unsupported, so the raw API answers HTTP 400. Rewrite: drop both keywords and state the 0..2 range in the field description or instructions. Enforcement is kept because validateDecision already rejects price outside [0,2] (src/agent/protocol.ts:86-87), but the model is no longer constrained, so an out-of-range price becomes a failed decision rather than an impossible one. Everything else is inside the documented subset. Objects use additionalProperties:false with every property required, giving 0 optional parameters against a limit of 24. One-value typed enums are supported (string and number enums are documented; the docs' own examples include an integer enum). Strings use enum only, with no pattern, length bounds, type arrays, $ref or allOf. anyOf with a {type:'null'} branch is allowed (anyOf and the null type are both listed). Union-type parameters, counted from src/agent/mockProvider.ts: move, communication, proximityUtterance.referent, proximityUtterance.context, diary, diary.context and role, so at most 7 against a limit of 16. Open risks, none settled by the docs. (1) The page says unions carry 'exponential compilation cost', and nested anyOf (communication > proximityUtterance > referent) plus a move anyOf with one object branch per legal move could hit 'Schema is too complex' or slow compilation. No enum-size cap is documented. (2) The 16-hex enums change per call, so the 24 h grammar cache mostly misses and nearly every call pays compile latency, which the docs do not quantify. Our code caps a call at 12,000 ms (src/agent/broker.ts:48, src/agent/responsesTransport.ts, src/agent/accountedBroker.ts:64), not the ~16 s in the stated facts. (3) Enum casing is not guaranteed; the docs describe it as typically the first letter after a space, so hex ids are at low risk, but member() in the validator is an exact match. Lowercase before comparing, or treat a mismatch as a failed read. Transport is not reusable: the Responses body does not map. A new adapter must POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages with the x-api-key and anthropic-version: 2023-06-01 headers (as in the docs' cURL example) and body {model, max_tokens, system, messages:[{role:'user',...}], output_config:{format:{type:'json_schema', schema}, effort:'low'}}. Drop text.format name/strict, reasoning, service_tier:'default' (Anthropic's values are auto/standard_only) and store. Read the answer from the content block of type 'text', since thinking blocks may precede it, and check stop_reason for 'refusal' and 'max_tokens'. Thinking tokens count against max_tokens, and our cap is 2,048 (src/agent/broker.ts:48), so either send thinking:{type:'disabled'} (allowed at low effort) or accept truncation risk. Sampling parameters cannot be set and no seed exists, so runs are not reproducible; replay has to use recorded responses. The model-id regex accepts 'claude-haiku-5-5'. Nothing here has been accepted by the live API; the first request must carry the real schema.

Same blocking item as Haiku 5.5: minimum/maximum on bakerPrice.price returns a 400 and must be dropped, with the range checked client-side by validateDecision (src/agent/protocol.ts:86-87). The rest of the schema is inside the same documented subset, with the same limits and the same open compile-latency, nested-anyOf and enum-casing risks. It also needs the same native /v1/messages adapter. Differences: no effort parameter, and thinking is off unless budget_tokens is sent (minimum 1,024), so nothing eats the 2,048 output cap and the refusal classifiers described for Haiku 5.5 are not documented for it. Temperature and top_p are probably settable, though no page states this outright. The cost is 10x Haiku 5.5, it is a legacy model, and its 'not sooner than' retirement date has already passed. It has no schema advantage over Haiku 5.5.

notes: Method. On 2026-10-22 (about 02:00-02:25 UTC) I fetched the .md rendering of each cited platform.claude.com docs page, plus claude.com/pricing as HTML, and read them directly. I did not use the researcher's saved copies. The cited .../api/openai-sdk URL redirects to .../cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/openai-sdk. No new research was done, no paid API calls were made, and no models, providers or runtimes outside the researcher's two were looked at.

Overall result. Every price, model id, date, tier, reasoning-control and schema-keyword claim I checked matches the source. Two minor corrections: the refusal categories are four (cyber, frontier_llm, bio, general_harms), not two, and the 1,024-token budget_tokens minimum for Haiku 4.5 is on the extended-thinking page, not the thinking page the researcher cited. Two items cannot be verified from docs: per-call latency with grammar compile, and how this workload tokenizes under Claude's tokenizer.

Blocking item. minimum/maximum on the Baker price is not supported by Anthropic and returns a 400 on the raw API. Neither Anthropic model can take the current schema unchanged. The fix is small (drop both keywords) because the validator already enforces 0..2. The 'const is already gone' change is irrelevant here; Anthropic supports const anyway.

Discrepancy with the stated facts. Those facts say ~16 s per call. The code I read caps a call at 12,000 ms (src/agent/broker.ts:48 rejects deadlineMs > 12_000; responsesTransport.ts and accountedBroker.ts use 12_000), and also caps maxOutputTokens at 2,048. Latency including grammar compile is the main unknown, so re-check which limit applies before judging the pilot.

Refusal risk is new on Haiku 5.5 relative to Haiku 4.5. general_harms and cyber classifiers can fire on benign work and return HTTP 200 with stop_reason 'refusal', billed, with no fallback. The game has deception-themed roles; whether that triggers a classifier is an untested guess, so treat a refusal as a failed decision and count it in the pilot.

Haiku 4.5 is dominated by Haiku 5.5 on price (10x), currency and retirement window. It stays a survivor only because no hard requirement is violated. Its 'not sooner than 2026-10-15' date has passed with no deprecation notice listed, and the docs promise at least 60 days' notice, so a retirement inside the study window is possible but not signalled.
Changing the model is a change of study condition, not a cost saving. Anthropic fixes the sampling parameters on Haiku 5.5, so there is no temperature or seed to pin.
If US-only processing is required, add 1.1x to every Haiku 5.5 price. Batch is 50% off but is asynchronous (up to 24 h) and cannot meet a per-call deadline.

Nothing here shows that any provider accepts this schema. Anthropic's docs say it should after the min/max change, but the first request with the real schema and a real count_tokens measurement is the only evidence that counts. Compile latency, 'Schema is too complex' and nested-anyOf behaviour can only be seen live.
